flagship.headline: The Beatles cut Love Me Do with Ringo on drums
flagship.summary_line_1: The Beatles held their first proper recording session at EMI's Abbey Road Studios, Ringo Starr's first date with the band, cutting Love Me Do and How Do You Do It under producer George Martin.
flagship.summary_line_2: The Ringo-drummed take of Love Me Do recorded that afternoon was chosen for the band's debut single, the opening shot of Beatlemania.

events.headline: The Youngbloods get bounced from The Tonight Show
events.summary_line_1: Folk rock band the Youngbloods were pulled from their scheduled slot on The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson after a shouting match with the crew during afternoon rehearsal.
events.summary_line_2: Carson sent them home on the air that night, a rare public flop for a band riding the reissued Get Together into the Top 5.

events.headline: The Beatles film the Hey Jude promo
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles spent the afternoon at Twickenham Film Studios filming color promotional clips for Hey Jude and Revolution, singing live over the backing tracks to dodge a Musicians' Union miming ban.
events.summary_line_2: Around 300 fans were brought in for the singalong finale, giving the band its first audience in over two years and the spark that led straight into the Get Back project.

events.headline: The Doors release People Are Strange
events.summary_line_1: Elektra Records released the Doors' People Are Strange, written by Jim Morrison and Robby Krieger after a late-night walk through Laurel Canyon.
events.summary_line_2: The song's tack piano and theatrical unease pushed it to No. 12 on the Hot 100, cementing the band's place in psychedelic rock.

events.headline: The first Jerry Lewis MDA Telethon goes on the air
events.summary_line_1: The first Jerry Lewis Labor Day Telethon for the Muscular Dystrophy Association began broadcasting from New York's Americana Hotel, running through the night into Labor Day.
events.summary_line_2: A single independent station carried it that first year, but the broadcast raised over a million dollars in pledges and grew into a decades-long television institution.

events.headline: The Beatles' Help! hits No. 1
events.summary_line_1: Help!, the title track from the Beatles' second film, reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, the band's ninth chart-topper in the United States.
events.summary_line_2: It held the top spot for three weeks, right at the peak of international Beatlemania.

events.headline: The Animals make their first US concert
events.summary_line_1: The Animals played their first-ever American show at the Paramount Theatre in Brooklyn, reopened especially for the booking, just as House of the Rising Sun sat at No. 1 on the Hot 100.
events.summary_line_2: The date kicked off the band's first US tour and helped establish the Animals as one of the heaviest-sounding acts of the British Invasion.

events.headline: The Beach Boys sign autographs and play Denver
events.summary_line_1: The Beach Boys drew crowds to a Woolworth's autograph session at Denver's Cherry Creek Shopping Center before playing the Moonlight Ballroom at Lakeside Amusement Park.
events.summary_line_2: Teenage fans packed both stops, signing copies of Surfin' Safari and Surfin' U.S.A. as the band's early surf-pop fame hit full stride.

events.headline: Murray the K's Holiday Revue packs the Brooklyn Fox
events.summary_line_1: DJ Murray the K's Holiday Revue rolled on at the Brooklyn Fox Theatre with a bill stacked with the Ronettes, Stevie Wonder, Ben E. King, the Miracles, and Jan and Dean.
events.summary_line_2: Package shows like this one threw R&B, soul, and pop acts onto the same stage for the same audience, a format that shaped how 1960s pop was sold live.

events.headline: The Beatles cut Love Me Do with Ringo on drums
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles held their first proper recording session at EMI's Abbey Road Studios, Ringo Starr's first date with the band, cutting Love Me Do and How Do You Do It under producer George Martin.
events.summary_line_2: The Ringo-drummed take of Love Me Do recorded that afternoon was chosen for the band's debut single, the opening shot of Beatlemania.

events.headline: The Highwaymen's Michael hits No. 1
events.summary_line_1: The Wesleyan University folk quintet the Highwaymen reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 with Michael, a 19th-century spiritual they'd adapted for their debut album.
events.summary_line_2: The gold-selling single held the top spot for two weeks and helped drive the collegiate folk boom of the early 1960s.

events.headline: Please Mr. Postman debuts on the Hot 100
events.summary_line_1: The Marvelettes' debut single Please Mr. Postman entered the Billboard Hot 100, the first chart appearance for the girl group and for the young Tamla label.
events.summary_line_2: The song climbed to No. 1 by December, becoming Motown's first-ever pop chart-topper.

events.headline: Ray Charles no-show sparks a riot in Portland
events.summary_line_1: Ray Charles failed to appear for a scheduled headline show at Portland's Royal Ballroom, and the waiting crowd tore the venue apart, drawing police and fire hoses.
events.summary_line_2: The incident, caught on film, showed just how volatile the era's touring circuit could get and how devoted Charles's Pacific Northwest fans already were.

events.headline: Judy Garland returns to the London Palladium
events.summary_line_1: Judy Garland gave her second one-woman show at the London Palladium, a triumphant return to the stage less than a year after a near-fatal bout with hepatitis.
events.summary_line_2: The two-act solo concert format she built for these shows became the template other pop vocalists followed for decades.

events.headline: Future Soundgarden guitarist Kim Thayil is born
events.summary_line_1: Kim Thayil was born in Seattle to Indian American parents, growing up to co-found Soundgarden and become one of grunge's defining lead guitarists.
events.summary_line_2: His drop-D riffs and odd time signatures, built on a childhood diet of heavy rock and free jazz, would help define the Seattle sound decades later.
